[OpenPFC / Learn by doing]{.lesson-kicker}

# A few lines. A mathematical idea. An answer you can check.

[Start with a derivative. Follow it into a heat equation. Change the numerical method and discover what changes in the answer.]{.lesson-deck}

:::

These lessons are invitations to experiment with C++ and OpenPFC. Each one
develops a small mathematical argument, shows the actual implementation,
and gives you a way to decide whether the answer is right. Read the source,
change a parameter, and try to predict the result before running it.

## Start with a question

For a first C++ program, start by [giving a grid physical meaning](geometry/first-domain/index.qmd).
Then let that grid carry a field and a numerical question.

Begin with [How accurately can we differentiate?](differentiation/periodic/index.qmd).
Second-order differences, fourth-order differences, and Fourier derivatives
act on the same smooth function. A refinement plot makes their different
behaviour visible.

Then follow one heat equation through three implementations:
[neighbouring values](heat/finite-differences/index.qmd),
[Fourier modes](heat/fourier/index.qmd), and
[an exact exponential propagator](heat/exponential/index.qmd).
The geometry and initial condition stay fixed, so each change in the answer
has a numerical explanation.

::: {#listing}
:::

Read [An FFT index is not a wave number](fourier/symbols/index.qmd) to connect
array indices, physical units and the Nyquist derivative convention.

Follow [a spreading Gaussian pulse](heat/gaussian-pulse/index.qmd) to distinguish
conserved discrete mass, spatial sampling and time-stepping accuracy.

## Make your first change

Install a compatible OpenPFC SDK and CLI using the
[installation guide](https://vtt-propertune.github.io/OpenPFC/docs/project/install/).
Run `openpfc doctor` once in your compiler/MPI environment. The
[CLI guide](https://vtt-propertune.github.io/OpenPFC/docs/user_guide/cli/)
explains SDK selection when it is not discovered automatically.

From the OpenPFC checkout:

```sh
cd examples/differentiation/periodic
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --launcher=none
```

Edit `input.json` to change the grid. Edit `model.cpp` to change the
function. The CLI compiles the model, preserves an attempt directory,
and prints its location. CSV files are in that attempt's `results/`.
Changing the input alone reuses the compiled executable.

The heat lessons share a small header for inputs and diagnostics. Their
commands add `--source-root ..` so that the CLI also preserves that header.
Each chapter gives the complete command. For MPI-capable chapters, invoke
the CLI once with `--ranks=2 --launcher=mpirun` instead of `--launcher=none`.
The complete-domain polynomial references and geometry-only programs use
the documented single-process command.

## Build a model you can configure and inspect

Write [initial patterns as callables](initialization/patterns/index.qmd),
then [select one through a native catalog](initialization/catalog/index.qmd).
A [JSON/TOML session](configuration/session/index.qmd) assembles the clock
and stack while keeping the physics callback visible. Compare
[implicit heat](heat/implicit-euler/index.qmd) with the other heat methods,
then follow [driver hook ordering](heat/driver-hooks/index.qmd).

Give the computed array a durable form with
[collective binary I/O](output/binary-field/index.qmd) and
[a geometry-aware result series](output/vtk-series/index.qmd).
The [Cahn–Hilliard lesson](phase-fields/cahn-hilliard/index.qmd) brings
state declaration, spectral symbols and a nonlinear local law together.

## Where next?

The [geometry sequence](geometry/decomposition/index.qmd) explains owned
boxes, [memory offsets](geometry/index-boxes/index.qmd),
[padded fields](geometry/field-storage/index.qmd), and
[physical-coordinate initialization](geometry/coordinate-fields/index.qmd).
Then use [a polar-defined pattern](geometry/polar-patterns/index.qmd) to
give those Cartesian points a different mathematical interpretation.
For the transform itself, compare [complex coefficients](fourier/round-trip/index.qmd)
and [local versus distributed layouts](fourier/field-layout/index.qmd).

The book-inspired sequence continues with
[cardinal interpolation](interpolation/cardinal/index.qmd),
[matrix and FFT differentiation](differentiation/collocation/index.qmd),
and [four regularity classes](differentiation/smoothness/index.qmd).
The latter includes the complete resolution presets for Trefethen's
programs 1, 2, and 7, alongside the hat and smooth-profile comparison of
programs 4 and 5.

Follow [a variable-speed wave](waves/variable-transport/index.qmd), then ask
[which timesteps are stable](integration/stability/index.qmd). On a finite
interval, begin with [where to place polynomial samples](polynomials/interpolation/index.qmd)
and work through [cosine-mapped differentiation](polynomials/differentiation/index.qmd),
[integration as an ODE](polynomials/integration/index.qmd),
[boundary equations](polynomials/boundary-values/index.qmd), and
[a nonlinear solve](polynomials/nonlinear-boundary/index.qmd).

Watch a pulse [reflect on an interval](waves/chebyshev-line/index.qmd),
[spread across a square](waves/chebyshev-square/index.qmd), and travel
through [a mixed Fourier–Chebyshev tank](waves/mixed-tank/index.qmd).
Then separate linear dispersion from nonlinear interaction in
[KdV](waves/kdv/index.qmd). The Allen–Cahn pair compares
[fixed lifted boundaries](polynomials/allen-cahn-fixed/index.qmd) with
[an explicitly driven endpoint](polynomials/allen-cahn-driven/index.qmd).
For another MPI storage choice, return to the heat equation with
[a compact core and separate halos](heat/separated-halos/index.qmd).

The [coverage inventory](coverage.qmd) lists every existing executable and
all forty book programs, including those still awaiting a teaching chapter.

To build a complete simulation workflow, investigate
[adaptive step rejection](integration/adaptive-rk/index.qmd),
[exponential step doubling](integration/adaptive-etd/index.qmd),
[output-time alignment](integration/output-clock/index.qmd),
[two fields at one RK stage](coupling/runtime-fields/index.qmd), and
[checkpoint restart](output/checkpoint-restart/index.qmd).
The [host orchestrator](coupling/host-orchestrator/index.qmd) shows how another
solver can own the loop. Start parallel work with
[MPI ownership](parallel/hello/index.qmd) and finish with
[structured diagnostics](diagnostics/profiling/index.qmd).

For operator and boundary problems, begin with
[harmonic-trap energies](fourier/harmonic-oscillator/index.qmd) and
[a periodic Mathieu potential](fourier/mathieu/index.qmd).
Then distinguish [physical and grid-scale eigenmodes](polynomials/eigenmodes/index.qmd)
before examining [the Airy constraint](polynomials/airy/index.qmd) and
[a perturbed membrane](polynomials/membrane/index.qmd).
The [square Poisson](polynomials/poisson-square/index.qmd),
[Helmholtz](polynomials/helmholtz-square/index.qmd), and
[boundary-driven Laplace](polynomials/laplace-square/index.qmd) sequence
shares one native tensor-action GMRES solve.
[Geometric multigrid](elliptic/multigrid/index.qmd) introduces a native
hierarchy on uniform grids. For a different use of complex arithmetic,
try [a contour integral](quadrature/complex-contour/index.qmd).
Continue to fourth-order problems with
[a clamped beam](polynomials/clamped-beam/index.qmd) and
[twenty-five square-plate modes](polynomials/clamped-plate/index.qmd).
Both build on native Chebyshev differentiation; the plate uses symmetry
to explain repeated vibration frequencies.
The [Orr–Sommerfeld problem](polynomials/orr-sommerfeld/index.qmd) reuses
the clamped operators to ask whether a small flow disturbance grows.
Its complex generalized eigenproblem separates matrix residuals from
resolution and stability.
For the sensitivity behind that distinction, examine
[pseudospectra of a complex oscillator](polynomials/pseudospectra/index.qmd).
Small singular values show where a small perturbation can move an eigenvalue.
The final book pair moves to a disk:
[vibration modes](polynomials/disk-modes/index.qmd) explain signed radii
and angular multiplicity, and [Poisson's equation](polynomials/poisson-disk/index.qmd)
uses an exact reference to distinguish a tiny residual from radial
approximation error.

The [existing examples catalogue](https://vtt-propertune.github.io/OpenPFC/docs/reference/examples_catalog/)
also includes adaptive integration, Cahn–Hilliard evolution, custom initial
conditions, coupled fields, and output. Those remain useful next steps after
these lessons. GPU execution has its own application/build path;
the source-model CLI used here currently qualifies CPU execution.

:::
